did_you_know.text: The exact locations of Pi-hahiroth and Baal-zephon are unknown today, so scholars have suggested several possible sites.
The word “shalishim” is sometimes understood as high-ranking officers or special chariot warriors, but its exact meaning is uncertain.
The phrase “and you shall be silent” does not refer to plowing; it means to keep quiet and not panic.
The passage moves from “stand firm” to “go forward,” suggesting that faith can involve not only waiting, but also taking a brave step.
The pillar of cloud, which had been in front of the camp, moves behind it to protect the Israelites from the Egyptians.
The same cloud brings darkness to one side and light to the other, showing how one situation can look different to opposing groups.
“Ruach kedem” means an east wind; the word “kedem” is connected with the east, where the sun rises.
“The morning watch” was probably the last division of the night, shortly before dawn.
War chariots depended heavily on their wheels; when the wheels stopped working, Egypt’s military advantage disappeared.
The word “yir’u” can mean both fear and awe, so the verse describes a change in how the Israelites viewed God.
